page: Microsoft Azure D16ns_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dnv6 network-optimized family. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor using simultaneous multithreading. It features a clock speed of up to 4.2 GHz, 260 MB of L3 cache, and 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs. Storage operations rely entirely on remote network-attached disks, making it capable of attaching Azure Premium Storage. Networking features are central to the D16ns_v6 designation, though it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default.

Benchmark measurements position the D16ns_v6 primarily in the middle 50% across standard synthetic evaluations, such as Geekbench (1915 single-core, 11276 multi-core) and PassMark CPU (26468.23). However, specific instruction workloads show higher capability: single-threaded gzip compression (31.44 GB/sec) and Geekbench text processing (2637.0) rank in the top 25%. In machine learning workloads utilizing CPU matrix instructions, text generation on a small 135M parameter model reaches 404.96 tokens per second, placing it in the top 10%, while medium 7B model generation settles into the average range at 15.78 tokens per second.

From an infrastructure perspective, the D16ns_v6 provides a balanced compute-to-memory profile for general production requirements. Tradeoffs include the total absence of ephemeral local disk space, which necessitates reliance on remote volumes for all persistent and scratch storage. Given its balanced resource ratios and network capabilities, the instance fits web application serving, database nodes, CI/CD runners, and CPU-based lightweight inference workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D16ns_v6 is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Powered by an 8-core Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz with 260 MB L3 cache, it supports AVX-512 and Intel AMX vector instructions. The configuration contains no dedicated GPUs and lacks local storage, relying entirely on remote network-attached storage options like Premium Storage. Benchmarks demonstrate steady mid-tier execution across PassMark, Geekbench, and Redis operations, with distinct strengths in text processing, single-thread gzip compression, and small-model CPU LLM inference. D16ns_v6 is suited for web applications, enterprise microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and general relational database deployments requiring consistent CPU allocation without ephemeral storage requirements.
